audience.who: curious general viewers, teens to retirees, no science background assumed
audience.assumed_knowledge: everyday experience only; no equations, no school physics required
audience.motivation: finally understand something they have seen or used all their life
audience.watch_context: watching for the 'oh, that is why' moment, not for a lesson

narrator_role.identity: a curious friend who went and found out
narrator_role.authority_style: earned through evidence shown on screen, never claimed
narrator_role.relationship: asks the viewer's question out loud before answering it

technical_language.jargon_policy: use the real term once, then translate it immediately into an everyday picture
technical_language.equations: never on screen; describe the relationship in words
technical_language.analogy_preference: high; every mechanism gets one everyday analogy
technical_language.numbers: only numbers backed by accepted research claims, always with a sense of scale

sentence_style.preferred_length: short to medium; one idea per sentence
sentence_style.spoken_rhythm: written to be heard: contractions, questions, short pauses

storytelling.structure: everyday moment -> surprising question -> wrong common answer -> hidden mechanism revealed in steps -> payoff that changes how the viewer sees the everyday thing
storytelling.hook: open on the thing the viewer already knows, then break their expectation within the first two sentences
storytelling.human_stakes: show who is affected: the pilot, the driver, the tuner, the viewer at home
storytelling.mystery: high; hold the core reveal until the mechanism is earned
storytelling.storytime_format: first-person stories only when the creator supplied the real story or a documented source is credited; never invented
